name: Cemex, S.A.B. de C.V.
moat_justification: Local cement/aggregates density, quarry and plant scarcity and high transport costs give Cemex pricing power in its core local markets, but the product is a commodity, ROIC has run only about 4-10% through the cycle and gross margin about 31-34%, and earnings ride construction cycles, energy/carbon costs and FX.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 22 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base

FX_CONVERTED: reporting currency MXN converted to USD at period-end ECB reference rates (frankfurter.app) — flow facts use the period-end rate, not a period average; the rates used are recorded in dcf_numbers.json fx_conversion
USD_TRANSLATIONS_USED: the issuer files its own USD convenience translations alongside its reporting currency; the engine used the filed USD figures

ADS_RATIO_APPLIED: 20-F filer — per-share figures scaled x30.0 ordinary shares per ADS (Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024, audited consolidated financial statements, Note 1 Description of Business: each CPO represents two series A shares and one series B share of common stock (3 ordinary shares per CPO), and each ADS represents ten CPOs - 30 ordinary shares per ADS. Corroborated in the same statements, Note 21: 662 million own shares cancelled in 2022 were stated as 22.1 million ADSs (662/22.1 is about 30).) so they are comparable to the ADS price; TTM pins are taken as per-ADS already

OVERRIDE_APPLIED:sbc — filing gap in the last 3 FY filled by a judgment override (filing: Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024, audited consolidated financial statements, Note 22 Executive Share-Based Compensation: the combined compensation expense for the Share-Based Compensation Programs amounted to $55 million in 2024, $61 million in 2023 and $52 million in 2022 (statements presented in millions of U.S. dollars)); an override never replaces a filed value — see overrides_applied and override_impact
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.5x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
HIGH_NET_DEBT: net debt is 8.6x normalized OE — levered OE can vanish fast; stress the bear cases
one_liner: Tier D: moat 5/10 local-density cement incumbent with ROIC of roughly 4-10% - on the last filed year (FY2024, 22 months stale, base $0.37/ADS once engine 5.5 adds intangible-asset purchases to capex) the weighted IRR is 7.03% at $10.26 with the whole band in D; clears 15% only at $3.59 (IV@15). A FY2025 base may lift it toward C, not near B.
exit_alert_suppressed_reason: tier exists only because of a judgment override
moat_for: Local market density: cement and aggregates are transport-cost bound (economic radius roughly 200-300km), so plant/quarry positions create local oligopolies
Scarce permitted quarry reserves and capital-intensive plants (over EUR150-200M per 1Mt of capacity) deter new entry
Proven local pricing power: Mexico cement prices rose in local currency in Q2 2026 prints while volumes also grew, and group gross margin has held about 33-34% in 2023-2024
Global scale across Mexico, the US and EMEA plus a ready-mix/aggregates distribution network that pulls through cement volumes
moat_against: ROIC proxy only 3.5-9.9% over 2022-2024 (fundamentals.json) and negative in 2020 - returns have not stayed well above the cost of capital through a cycle
Commodity product with no global pricing power: utilization runs the economics, so a small volume drop can erase profit (high operating leverage)
Gross margin has drifted down from about 36% in 2016 to about 33-34% - no expanding pricing-power trend
Energy, carbon (EU ETS/CBAM) and decarbonization capex are structural cost threats; cement is one of the most capital-intensive industries
MXN/USD and multi-currency exposure: a USD-priced ADS on largely non-USD earnings, plus recurring tax/legal overhangs (the Spanish tax assessments that hit 2023)

overrides.source: Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024, audited consolidated financial statements, Note 22 Executive Share-Based Compensation: the combined compensation expense for the Share-Based Compensation Programs amounted to $55 million in 2024, $61 million in 2023 and $52 million in 2022 (statements presented in millions of U.S. dollars)
